VIT uses relative grading for theory classes with more than 10 enrolled students. Contributor count does not tell us the full class strength. Smaller classes, labs, projects and soft skills use absolute grading.

Theory requires at least 40% in FAT; embedded courses also require at least 50% in the lab and combined total. An overall 50 or above secures at least E when the pass requirements are met.

Relative S predictions start at 80 or the calculated mean + 1.5 SD boundary, whichever is higher. Absolute S starts at 90. VIT’s special S rule for the top 3 students or top 5% with at least 80 needs the full ranked class and is not estimated here.

Relative ranges use a contributor sample. Official statistics use every student’s rounded-up total; the sample keeps fractional totals. Final university grades can differ.
